C0.quote: We study committee voting rules under ranked preferences
C0.note: Committee voting rules aggregating voters' rankings; axiomatic study.

C1.quote: no committee voting rule satisfies both committee monotonicity and Rank-JR
C1.note: Mostly axiomatic. Polynomial-time computability (Prop 5.4) is minor. Swap-distance bounds (Thm 8.3) are also treated as axiomatic/proportionality guarantees.

C2.1.quote: A preference profile 𝑅 is the collection of the voters’ preferences

C2.2.quote: voters submitting ranked preferences, potentially with indifferences (i.e., weak orders)
C2.2.note: Strict rankings, weak orders, truncated rankings. Approval is mentioned as a special case of weak preferences.

C2.3.quote: every voter 𝑖 ∈ 𝑁 reports a (weak) preference relation
C2.3.note: The paper speaks of voters' preferences throughout, but they are defined as what is reported.

C2.4.quote: every voter 𝑖 ∈ 𝑁 reports a (weak) preference relation
C2.4.note: Preferences are described as reported and the rule is applied to them directly. There is no statement on sincerity or on how they relate to held attitudes.

C3.1.note: No strategic analysis is given. Strategic behaviour is not analysed.

C3.2.note: No statement that voters submit their held attitudes.

C4.1.note: No utilities, welfare, satisfaction or cost are defined for voters. The word 'satisfaction' appears only as 'contributing to the satisfaction of N′', which is not a utility notion.

C4.2.note: The term is mentioned only in passing, as a parenthetical for the approval domain. It is not part of the paper's formal model, and no utility reading is given.

C5.1.quote: this group should be represented by a number of candidates in 𝐶 ′
C5.1.note: PSC and IPSC are proportional representation axioms for groups of voters. Swap distance for proportional rankings is also studied.

C5.2.quote: a committee voting rule satisfies PSC or IPSC if its selected committee always
C5.2.note: The criteria are evaluated on the submitted profile, with no statement relating it to held attitudes.

VOT.note: Voters appear only as providers of inputs. No actions are modelled as choices.

ORG.note: No organiser makes a choice in the model.

DES.note: The rule designer's choice is not modelled.

C7.1.note: Fewer than two types are present.

C8.1.note: NA: no type is STRAT or MIXED.

claims.quote: committee monotonicity is often a requirement because the number of winners is uncertain
this provides further motivation for using methods that satisfy our fairness conditions
it suggests that it may be impossible to attain stronger proportionality conditions than PSC

C9.1.note: Claims about applications such as lecturer, recommender and awards, and about which rules are suitable.

C9.2.quote: Proportionality is desirable in this context because topics should be chosen
C9.2.note: The claims about fairness towards voters and suitability for applications need the assumption that reported rankings reflect voters' true preferences. This assumption is not stated. A link between ordinal rankings and voters' interests is also needed and is not stated.

C10.1.note: No explicit procedural reading is stated.
